claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you have a 17-year-old son named Alex who lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. He finished school but he's not studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he has registered within the last 20 weeks after leaving education, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit during that period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few final questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16-19, this depends on them staying in approved education or training. Since Alex is 17 and:
- Is not in approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, A-levels, or an approved training program)
- Has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would have allowed Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education)

He does not meet the requirements for Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he enrolls in college, starts an approved training program, or registers with a careers service—you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit again at that point.

Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
